history.summary: KubeCoderDeploy's seven Build-Main pins now live only in config/{dev,prd}/values.yaml on build 523 — dev bare, prd prd-523 — with chart/values.yaml carrying no tag for them and the five container templates plus controller-config.yaml `required`-guarding their keys, so a stage missing one fails the render naming the key. tests/render-chart.py enforces the inverted invariant (chart names none, stage names exactly the seven, per-stage tag shape, one build within and across the stages, and a null-set render per key); twelve mutations each turn it red and `kc project test` and `kc project lint` are green. Committed as KubeCoderDeploy 49f0629 on phase/011-P1, plan done-record as AnsibleSpecs 5ceafee.

P1 meets its outcome: the seven pins live only in the stage files on build 523 (verified the newest dev-<n> the registry actually holds), chart/values.yaml names none, and the chart's required-guards genuinely fail a stage missing any one — proven by mutating both guards away, after which helm exits 0 rendering an untagged image and a null worker. The gate rewrite loses no prior coverage and its --set <path>=null check is a real, non-vacuous mutation test. No findings.

cicd.writeVersionPins(repo:, pins:, message:) lands in JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/cicd.groovy (482706a on phase/011-P2): it clones a deploy repo, rewrites the named YAML paths in the named values files surgically, and commits and pushes the whole set as one commit, erroring on a path the file does not already hold and committing nothing when nothing changed. The repo has no gate and this environment has no JVM (Ruling 2), so in its place I ran a line-for-line Python transcription of the rewrite (40 checks against P1's real stage files), a clone-edit-commit-push rehearsal against a local bare remote, sh -n on both emitted shell scripts and a delimiter check over the file - all green, and the transcription caught one real bug before commit.

writeVersionPins meets the phase's outcome — one commit for the whole set, surgical and idempotent writes, unknown/duplicate paths thrown before the commit, a no-op run that says so, and the estate's clone-edit-push credential pattern. One blocking defect: the values-file map is probed with the caller's raw key at :52 and read with a String-coerced key at :98, so a caller whose file paths are GStrings loses its pins — the GString-key hazard the file defends against on the inner map and reintroduces on the outer one. The branch is unverified (no gate, no JVM), and the Python transcription that stood in for a gate cannot reproduce this class of defect.

findings.summary: vars/cicd.groovy:98 reads pins[file] with a String-coerced key after :52 probed it with the caller's raw key, so a GString-keyed pins map resolves to null and that file's pins are never applied
the round-trip guarantee at vars/cicd.groovy:233-235 fails for a plain-styled line given an all-digit or boolean-like value, which YAML reads back as an int or a bool

history.summary: F1 confirmed and fixed: Groovy's map subscript coerces a GString key, so a pins dict built with an interpolated values-file path could be read by no subscript in writeVersionPins — the caller was told 'config/dev/values.yaml names no pins' about a file it had plainly named (F1's symmetric branch) and no pin landed. A new @NonCPS normalizePins() turns the whole structure — file paths, YAML paths and values — into real Strings at the entry, so applyPins needs no defence of its own and two spellings of one file name collide rather than silently dropping a file's pins. Witnessed and verified under a portable JVM plus groovy-all 2.4.21 (the version workflow-cps compiles): the method body against KubeCoderDeploy's real stage files with Jenkins steps stubbed — String-keyed and GString-keyed callers now write identical bytes, exactly the seven lines change per file, all fourteen values round-trip through a YAML parser as strings, a re-run pushes nothing, every guard throws before a write, and all seven vars/*.groovy parse. JenkinsPipelineUtils c5bf246; advisory F2 left standing (already close-out B2); close-out S4 records that a JVM is obtainable here, narrowing G2's premise.

Round-1's blocking F1 is resolved, witnessed by running vars/cicd.groovy unmodified under Temurin 17 + groovy-all 2.4.21 with Jenkins steps stubbed and a local bare remote seeded from P1's real stage files: the pre-fix commit fails the interpolated-key caller with 'config/dev/values.yaml names no pins', the fix commit writes all fourteen pins in one commit. Every applyPins guard survives the wanted->pins rename, V02 holds end to end (7 lines per file, nothing else touched, values round-trip as strings, a re-run pushes nothing), and all seven vars/*.groovy parse. One new finding, Minor and advisory: the duplicate-key guard this commit adds covers the values-file map and not the pins map.

findings.summary: normalizePins throws on a values file named twice (:154-157) but silently collapses two keys naming one YAML path (:161), dropping a pin with a success return.

history.summary: Every requirement and ruling the plan states has implementing work I can point at: R1 in cicd.writeVersionPins (P2), R5/R6/R7 in KubeCoderDeploy's stage-file pins, chart required-guards and rewritten render gate (P1), R8 and Ruling 5 in design.md's three sites, D45/D37's amendments and slice 012's carried-in section (P3); R2/R4 left the slice under Ruling 1 and R3 is discharged as evidence, not a change (G4). V04 — Ruling 2's library-load canary — is the only unimplemented criterion and is the test phase's to prepare, which runs after this consult. The three advisory findings the P3 review left do not clear the bar: S5 is plan-described but its three constraints are already stated in the method's own docstring, which is what the author of the slice-012 call reads, and Ruling 5's enumerated handoff all landed; S6's contradiction is Ruling 1's own staging against G5, and both texts now sit in slice 012's slice.md for its planner to settle; both are noted in the close-out rather than bought with an executor round, a review round and another consult. B4's two false absolutes in the register were mechanical prose residue in files this slice already touched — fixed and committed here (AnsibleSpecs a4fd09c), B4 struck, with S2 and B1's stale build-511 numbers noted against Ruling 4's 523.

Ran the strategy end to end: the driver's sweep was green and not re-run, and I verified the work itself — the real `writeVersionPins` body and its emitted shell executed against a local bare remote (one commit, exactly the 7 pin lines per file, a repeat run pushes nothing, every guard throws, the token is in neither the console nor the history), the chart's missing-pin guards (14/14 renders refused naming the key), the gate (17 mutations, none blind), all seven vars/*.groovy through groovy-all 2.4.21 and groovy-cps 1.31's CpsTransformer, the registry (dev-523 held for all seven; 523/prd-523 are the accepted forward references) and the register/slice-012 edits: 11 of 12 verification items pass, one comment-only fix was committed (JenkinsPipelineUtils 2c43b06), and KubeCoderDeploy 49f0629, JenkinsPipelineUtils 2c43b06 and AnsibleSpecs 08c962c are pushed (Ansible has no slice commits, so no iac-on-push run applies). Deploy-owed: nothing to apply, since no role, playbook, inventory or Terraform module changed; the one item owed to the operator is V04, Ruling 2's canary — Build Now on https://jenkins.webathome.org/job/AaC/job/Ansible/ and hand back the console, which must show `Resolved main as branch main at revision 2c43b0694cd94e66942644b9504d4690bed44f38` and finish SUCCESS (close-out A1).
